question:
Using the inverse-matrix method, solve the system
$$3x+2y=13$$
$$x-y=1$$

(a) Express the system in the form $AX=B$ and show that $A$ is invertible.

(b) Find $A^{-1}$ and hence determine $x$ and $y$.

(c) Verify the solution in both equations.
explanation:
(a)
The system can be written as
$$AX=B$$
where
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2\\1 & -1\end{bmatrix},\quad X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}13\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Now,
$$|A|=3(-1)-2(1)=-5\neq0$$
Therefore, $A$ is invertible.

(b)
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{-5}\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -2\\-1 & 3\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\1 & -3\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$X=A^{-1}B$$
$$X=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\1 & -3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}13\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
$$X=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}15\\10\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\2\end{bmatrix}$$
Hence, $x=3$ and $y=2$.

(c)
Substituting $x=3$ and $y=2$,
$$3(3)+2(2)=9+4=13$$
$$3-2=1$$
Thus, the solution is verified.

options.B:
(a) $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&2\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=-5$
(b) $A^{-1}=\frac15\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\1&-3\end{bmatrix}$ and $(x,y)=(2,3)$
(c) Only the second equation is satisfied
options.D:
(a) $|A|=0$, so $A$ is singular
(b) $A^{-1}$ does not exist
(c) The system has no solution
